Investment Bank: A financial institution that helps companies raise capital and advises on major transactions like M&A and IPOs. NOT the same as a retail or commercial bank.
M&A: Mergers and Acquisitions. A merger is when two companies combine into one. An acquisition is when one company purchases another.
Buy-Side: In M&A advisory, the bank advising the company that wants to BUY (acquire) another company.
Sell-Side: In M&A advisory, the bank advising the company that is being SOLD or wants to find a buyer.
IPO: Initial Public Offering. The first time a private company sells shares to the public on a stock exchange. The investment bank manages this entire process.
Underwriting: When an investment bank agrees to buy all shares from a company at the IPO price and then resells them to investors. The bank takes on the risk.
Spread: The underwriting fee — typically 3–7% of total IPO proceeds — that the bank earns for taking on the underwriting risk.
Due Diligence: Deep analysis of a target company's financials, legal situation, risks, and operations before a deal closes.
Pitch Book: A presentation deck created by investment bankers to pitch their services to potential clients or to pitch a deal to potential buyers.
Analyst: The most junior banker. Responsible for building financial models, updating pitch books, and pulling comparable company data.
Associate: Mid-level banker who reviews and refines models, writes memos, and bridges the gap between Analysts and VPs.
Vice President (VP): Senior banker who manages deal execution day-to-day, oversees timelines, and handles client communication.
Managing Director (MD): The most senior deal team member. Responsible for bringing in new clients and closing deals.
Capital Markets: One of the two main IB functions. Helps companies raise money through equity offerings (like IPOs) or debt (bonds).
Advisory: One of the two main IB functions. Providing strategic advice on mergers, acquisitions, and other major financial transactions.
Roadshow: Before an IPO, the company and its bankers tour major cities to pitch the investment to institutional investors.
Book Building: The process of collecting buy orders from investors to determine the final IPO price range.
Mandate: When a company formally hires an investment bank to advise on or execute a deal.
Tombstone: An advertisement placed by investment banks announcing a completed deal. Named for their rectangular, grave-marker appearance.
Chinese Wall: An information barrier within a bank that prevents the flow of information between different departments (e.g., M&A and trading).
